learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of energy conversion and the types of fluid machines (drivers and driven).
Analyze real thermodynamic transformations and calculate performance parameters (efficiency, specific fuel consumption).
Assess energy system performance under varying operating conditions.
Critically compare different plant configurations and select fluid machines for specific applications.
Present evaluations and comparisons effectively using graphical and numerical representations.

syllabus_topics: Energy demand, sources, and conversion processes
Thermodynamic fundamentals: mass and energy balances, ideal gas transformations, property calculations
Hydrocarbon combustion: stoichiometric air calculation, calorific values
Energy systems and fluid machines: types, classification, and components
Thermodynamic cycles: ideal, limiting, and real; work and heat exchange calculations (Rankine, Joule, Otto, Diesel, Sabathé)
Fluid flow in ducts, compression and expansion processes, sonic conditions
Gas turbine plants: components, cycle variants, Joule cycle optimization
Steam plants: ideal and real cycles, regeneration, reheating, boilers, condensers, cooling towers
Internal combustion engines: ideal and real cycles, losses, supercharging, performance curves
Combined-cycle and cogeneration systems: performance indices (IRE, PES)
Renewable energy conversion: hydroelectric, photovoltaic, bioenergy systems
Fluid machines: pumps, compressors, fans, turbines; classification, similarity laws, characteristic curves, cavitation
Overview of energy cost and utilization factor
Quantitative analysis of performance and thermodynamic parameters
teaching_methods: Lectures supported by slides and schematic diagrams
Numerical exercises to apply theoretical concepts and develop calculation skills
Presentation of quantitative examples and calculation procedures

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (one numerical exercise, five structured questions, two open questions)
Oral exam (two questions on theory and practical applications)

assessment_rules: The written exam requires the numerical exercise to be correct and a minimum score on structured questions. The oral exam comprises two questions, each requiring a score of at least 18/30. The final grade is the average of the two oral questions.
